task: This is a synthetic newspaper-writing exercise using fictional reporting notes. Use only the supplied reporting notes. Write from the reporting snapshot as of August 18, 2026. Write a headline and a 450–650-word AP-style reported feature about the early food counter at Selwick Ferry Terminal and how a small vendor's timetable intersects with the working day on the waterfront.

facts.text: An Aug. 18, 2026, terminal note records food-counter owner Ceri Lann packing preordered breakfast rolls before the first ferry crew's boarding call.
Lann extended opening from 7 a.m. to 5:45 a.m. in May to serve terminal and vessel workers.
The terminal's first staff shifts begin at 5:30 a.m., while most nearby shops open after 8 a.m.
Workers can bring their own food, but their opportunities to leave the secure work area depend on duties and sailing schedules.
The ferry operator is running a six-week pilot offering 40 eligible early-shift employees a $5 food voucher per worked shift.
The voucher can be used at Lann's counter before 9 a.m. and is not a cash payment added to wages.
The posted $6.50 breakfast package price includes any applicable tax; one $5 voucher leaves the worker paying $1.50.
Unused pilot vouchers expire on their issue day and are not available to every person working around the harbor.
The operator reimburses redeemed vouchers to Lann every 14 days, creating a gap between providing food and receiving that part of the payment.
Lann pays suppliers weekly and says early-opening labor costs continue even when a sailing is canceled.
The kiosk's rent is $850 a month, with electricity billed separately.
Lann said, "A voucher is a sale I have made, but it is not cash I can hand to the bread supplier that morning."
Deck worker Omi Darsen sometimes orders ahead because boarding checks can leave only a short collection window.
Darsen said, "The useful part is knowing the food is ready when the gap in the work appears."
The terminal has a staff break room, but its opening does not guarantee that all jobs can pause at the same time.
The operator has not published evidence that the voucher pilot improved attendance, productivity or health.
Lann has not provided a complete profit comparison for the early counter hours.
The pilot will be reviewed after six weeks, with no commitment yet to extend it to later shifts or other vendors.
The counter occupies a former ticket-information booth and uses an insulated collection shelf for completed orders.
The reporting record gives no change to sailing times, security access rules or workers' contractual break entitlements.

forbidden_additions: Cash wage increases, vouchers for every harbor worker or guaranteed free meals
Proven health or productivity benefits, changed break rights or a permanently funded program
